issues.title: Renew the lease while a suite runs, and stop when it is gone
issues.body:
## The gap

The worker **never heartbeated.** A suite runs for minutes; the lease is finite. Nothing renewed it.

So a slow machine or a longer suite lets the lease lapse mid-run, another worker takes the task, and this one finishes, tries to submit, and gets `lease-owner-mismatch` — every minute of work discarded, with no message anyone would think to go looking for.

It happens to fit today because `check:syntax` takes 16 seconds against a 1800-second lease. That's margin, not a design.

## What changed

Renews once a minute while a suite runs (`RELAY_HEARTBEAT_MS`). If a renewal is **refused**, it kills the child rather than spending the remaining minutes producing a result it cannot submit.

A transient network error is **not** treated as a lost lease — only an explicit refusal counts. The two aren't the same, and guessing wrong throws away good work.

## Both branches proved live

**Renewal** — `test:deterministic` (~2 min), 20-second interval, issue #57:

```
claimed #57 attempt 1/3
renewed the lease 5 time(s) during #57
#57 -> RECEIVED
```

**Abort** — and here the obvious test *couldn't work*, which is worth reading.

I had a rival worker submit a competing result 40 seconds into a run. It was **refused** with `lease-owner-mismatch` (issue #58) — because an actively heartbeating worker still holds a live lease. The feature had made its own failure scenario unreachable. Good news, but it left the abort branch unproven.

So I forced the state instead: wrote the result comment directly, which is what `resolveLease` actually reads to decide a task is COMPLETED (issue #59):

```
claimed #59 attempt 1/3
lease lost mid-run on #59: task-already-completed -- aborting
abandoning #59: lease lost to another worker mid-run. No result submitted.
done; handled 0 task(s).
```

Killed the child, submitted nothing, didn't overwrite the other owner's history.

## One more thing worth knowing

A task created and polled seconds later can be **invisible** — GitHub's label index lags issue creation. My first heartbeat run reported `0 task(s) visible` for an issue I'd just made.

Not a defect here: the next scheduled run picks it up. But it looks exactly like a packet parse failure, and it isn't one — I verified the packet parses fine and the same poll returned it a minute later. Recording it so the next person doesn't spend an hour debugging their own code.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run check:syntax` | pass |
| `npm run test:deterministic` | **1191 tests, 1149 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped** |
| live renewal | #57, 5 renewals across a 2-minute suite |
| live theft attempt | #58, correctly refused |
| live abort | #59, detected, killed, submitted nothing |
| queue after | `IDLE`, 0 open |

Issues #57–#59 annotated with what each proved and closed. No external effect.

`lite/` untouched.

issues.title: Stop the worker reporting a killed suite as a failure, or a lost result as work done
issues.body:
Two defects, both the same kind: **a failure shaped like a success.**

## 1. A timed-out suite was reported as a failed one

`execFile` signals a timeout kill exactly like a non-zero exit. Nothing separated them, so a suite that never finished produced:

```
status/conf : FAILED / HIGH
test result : FAIL
truthTable  : {"deterministic":"FAILED"}
decision    : REPAIR
```

Every line is false. **The deterministic suite passes — 1191 tests, 0 failures.** It was killed, not failed. The receipt asserted a verification result it never obtained, at *high* confidence, and asked a reviewer to repair something that is fine.

That's the precise dishonesty the receipt contract exists to prevent, coming from the one producer nobody watches.

Now: `NOT_RUN`, `LOW`, `OWNER_REQUIRED`, and a limitation saying in plain words *"this is not evidence that the suite fails."*

### The first attempt at this fix didn't work

Worth recording rather than hiding. I tested `error.code === undefined`. Node sets it to **`null`** on a timeout kill — so the condition silently never matched and the bug shipped looking fixed. Issue #61 is the receipt it produced.

`killed === true` is the marker. I checked the real error object the second time instead of guessing again.

| | #61 (before) | #62 (after) |
|---|---|---|
| status / confidence | `FAILED` / `HIGH` | `FAILED` / `LOW` |
| test result | `FAIL` | `NOT_RUN` |
| truthTable | `FAILED` | `NOT_RUN` |
| decision | `REPAIR` | `OWNER_REQUIRED` |
| limitations | 2 | 3, including the explicit disclaimer |

## 2. A failed submit counted as handled work

`handled += 1` ran unconditionally. So a result that couldn't be filed:

- consumed a slot against `maxTasks` — the worker stopped early having accomplished nothing
- logged at normal level, as though the task were done

Meanwhile the lease lapses, the task strands, and **one of its three attempts is spent on work that completed and was thrown away.**

Now it logs `SUBMIT FAILED` at error level, counts nothing, and exits non-zero so a scheduler notices instead of recording a clean run. Proved on #63:

```
SUBMIT FAILED on #63: task-already-completed. The suite ran but its result
could not be filed; this attempt is lost and the task will strand.
done; handled 0 task(s), 1 submit failure(s).
exit code 1
```

Getting that scenario required care: an actively heartbeating worker can't lose its lease, so I used a short suite with the default 60s heartbeat — no renewal fires — and changed the task state mid-run.

## A correction

When I proposed this work I said a stale poll snapshot was the next bug. **It isn't.** `claimGithubRelayTask` re-reads the issue and its comments and refuses with `task-already-completed`, so the claim is the authority and the snapshot can't cause duplicate work. I checked before building anything, and found these two instead.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run check:syntax` | pass |
| `npm run test:deterministic` | **1191 tests, 1149 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped** |
| live | #61 old behaviour, #62 corrected, #63 submit loss |
| queue after | `IDLE`, 0 open |

Issues #61–#63 annotated and closed; #61 deliberately kept as the counter-example. No external effect.

`lite/` untouched.

issues.title: Fix the HTTP ingress: poll was broken, and receipts lost their provenance
issues.body:
The ingress had **never handled a real request.** Every test drove it with a fake client, so nothing had ever exercised the code that builds GitHub URLs or forwards a submit.

I ran it once against the real API. Two defects, immediately.

## 1. `poll` returned 400

The transport passes `state: 'OPEN'`. GitHub answers **422** for anything but lowercase:

```
OPEN   -> 422 {"message":"Validation Failed","errors":[{"value":"OPEN",...}]}
open   -> 200 []
```

**The operation ChatGPT uses to discover work at all was broken against the real API** — while the unit suite was green, because every fake accepted whatever it was handed.

Normalised at the client boundary, which is the layer that has to speak GitHub's dialect, rather than asking each caller to remember.

## 2. Receipt provenance was discarded in silence

Only `workerId`, `status` and `result` were forwarded. A caller that carefully supplied the rest got this:

| sent | filed |
|---|---|
| `sourceCommit: "deadbee"` | `"UNKNOWN"` |
| `confidence: "HIGH"` | `"UNKNOWN"` |
| `findings: [...]` | `[]` |
| `limitations: [...]` | `[]` |
| `duration: 1234` | `null` |

…and a **200 RECEIVED** in reply. Dropping evidence while reporting success is the worst failure this contract can have. Issue #65 captures it; #66 is the same request afterwards with every field intact.

## The fakes were the reason this hid

The tests now drive the **real client** through a fake `fetch`, and the fake **behaves like GitHub** — it returns 422 for a non-lowercase state, exactly as the API does.

A fake that says yes to everything isn't a test double, it's a way to keep a bug.

One new test exists for a failure mode worse than the 400: a validation error that becomes `200` with `count:0`, which reads as *"no work to do"* when the truth is *"the query was rejected"*. It pins that this fails loudly.

## Both tests verified by breaking the fix

A test that cannot fail is not protection, so I reverted each fix in turn:

```
revert lowercase fix  -> not ok 10 - poll asks GitHub for a lowercase state
revert provenance fix -> not ok 13 - submit forwards the provenance the caller sent
restored              -> 13 pass, 0 fail
```

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run check:syntax` | pass |
| `npm run test:deterministic` | **1195 tests, 1153 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped** |
| `tests/vercel-agent-relay.test.mjs` | 13/13 |
| live | #65 broken behaviour, #66 fixed, both closed |

## Still true

The ingress is **deployed nowhere.** This was driven over loopback against the real GitHub API, which exercises every line except the hosting. It does not become live until someone pastes credentials into Vercel — but it is now worth deploying, which it demonstrably wasn't an hour ago.

`lite/` untouched. No sends, spend, deploys, or credential changes.

issues.title: Scope pending agent result replay to the owning worker
issues.body:
## Why

PR #40's scheduler-safe worker tick scanned the global pending-result store with `limit: 1` and replayed the first record it saw before claiming new work. In a multi-worker deployment, that lets worker A replay worker B's already-computed result using A's callbacks/current budget configuration. That is a cross-worker identity and accounting failure mode.

## What this stacked PR changes

This PR is stacked directly on the current PR #40 head `d806f715223b6a4ec4babc70f1fa0606dccf294a`.

issues.title: Untrack a bad node_modules symlink, and discover the suites instead of listing them
issues.body:
Two fixes. The first is urgent and is my fault.

## A self-referential `node_modules` symlink is on `main`

`node_modules -> /home/user/uberbondd/node_modules` was committed in `d806f71`, one of my own commits. I created it with a worktree setup line that ran once with the working directory back at the repo root, then swept it into git with `git add -A`.

**Any checkout of `main` gets a `node_modules` that points at itself.** It shadows the real dependency tree, so npm cannot run a single script and every test dies with `Cannot find package 'pg'`.

Two things had to be wrong for it to land, and both are fixed:

- The symlink is untracked (`git rm --cached` — nobody's working copy is touched).
- `.gitignore` said `node_modules/` **with a trailing slash**, which matches a *directory*. A symlink named `node_modules` isn't one, so it was never ignored and `git add -A` took it without complaint. The slash is gone.

### I misdiagnosed this for an hour

When both gates started exiting 216 after the merges, I concluded the `package.json` script strings had outgrown npm and rewrote them. Wrong. The proof I should have run first: `npm run` on a script that was literally `node -e 'console.log("plain ok")'` **also exited 216**. No script could run, because no dependency existed. `main` was green the whole time.

## The suite refactor stands anyway, on its own evidence

| | files named | files reached | tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| old hand-maintained list | 116 | 135 | 1417 |
| discovered | 126 | 145 | **1567** |

**Ten test files had never executed under the main gate** — not by name, and not by import from anything named:

```
pending-relay-reconciliation   relay-deployment-attempt
relay-deployment-eligibility   relay-preview-integration
relay-preview-proof            relay-preview-runbook
relay-shadow-binding           relay-vercel-api-executor
relay-vercel-api-request       relay-zero-effects-contract
```

They arrived with #45, which put them in a separate `test:relay-safety` script that `npm run check` never calls. Discovery finds them because they exist. **+150 tests, all passing, that the gate was silently skipping.**

The runner also excludes any file another handed file imports, so the double-execution bug I introduced earlier is now structurally impossible rather than fixed once.

## The guard, rewritten around the same primitives

Every test file must execute somewhere · none may execute twice · browser and live-database suites stay out of the deterministic set · no script may drift back toward an unreasonable size.

That last one is explicitly a **canary, not a proof** — set at 2,000 characters, deliberately loose enough not to fail `test:relay-safety` at a legitimate 412. Inventing a rule isn't the same as protecting an invariant.

## Verification (after repairing `node_modules`)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run check:syntax` | 353 files parse, exit 0 |
| `npm run test:deterministic` | **1567 tests, 1525 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped** |
| `npm audit` | 0 vulnerabilities |

`lite/` untouched. No external effect.

issues.title: [P1][agent-mesh] Follow-up tasks can silently drop parent constraints
issues.body:
## Finding

Current `main` at `0ec8dd0842c845fa1c93229e9510d033d498ec05` still allows an autonomous child/follow-up task to omit custom constraints from its parent.

In `src/agent-autonomy-loop.mjs`, `ingestAgentResult()` builds the next intent with:

```js
constraints: coordination.constraints
```

while `compileTaskIntent()` adds only the two global defaults:

```js
local-preparation-only
no-business-external-effects
```

The parent task's custom constraints are not carried forward. `registerTaskIntent()` also stores no constraint snapshot in session history, so the later compiler cannot independently prove attenuation.

The relay adapter does add the fixed mandatory forbidden actions, which is good, but that does **not** preserve parent-specific restrictions such as protected paths, allowed repository scope, network restrictions, data-use restrictions, or a mission-specific prohibition.

## Why this matters

A model can return `ENGINEERING_REQUIRED` / `REPAIR_REQUIRED` / `RESEARCH_REQUIRED` with an empty or weaker `coordination.constraints` list. The follow-up then remains `LOCAL_PREPARATION`, but it can be less constrained than its parent.

This violates the intended rule:

> child authority may attenuate; it may never expand silently.

For an unattended GPT ↔ UberBond ↔ Claude loop, parent-to-child constraint loss is an authority-expansion failure mode.

## Required invariant

For every automatically generated child task:

```text
child.constraints ⊇ parent.constraints
child.forbiddenActions ⊇ parent.forbiddenActions
child consequence class <= parent consequence class
child/session budget <= remaining governed budget
```

Task-specific child constraints may be added, never used to delete inherited restrictions.

## Minimum regression

Create an initial intent with constraints such as:

```js
['protected-path:lite/', 'repo-scope:src/payments.mjs', 'network:none']
```

Have the worker request a safe follow-up with:

```js
coordination: {
  action: 'REPAIR_REQUIRED',
  objective: 'repair it',
  acceptanceTests: ['node --test'],
  constraints: []
}
```

Before the fix, the child loses all three restrictions.

After the fix, assert all parent restrictions remain and new child restrictions are unioned on top.

Also add a hostile case where the child supplies a contradictory/weaker-looking marker and prove it cannot remove the inherited entry.

## Suggested shape

Prefer one canonical inheritance/attenuation helper rather than duplicating rules in the autonomy loop and relay adapter. Persist enough immutable parent policy in the session/task lineage for restart-safe verification rather than relying only on caller memory.

Do not solve this by merely adding more fixed global constraints. The bug is loss of **mission-specific parent restrictions**.

## Verification required

- focused autonomy inheritance regression
- full deterministic suite
- mutation proof: temporarily remove the inheritance union and show the new test fails
- no `lite/` change
- zero external effects

## Boundaries

No provider calls, sends, spend, deployment, DNS, credentials, payments, KYC, customer mutation, or production mutation are required for this fix.

issues.title: [P1][agent-mesh] Autonomy pump can accept an incomplete unvalidated worker result as DONE
issues.body:
## Finding

Current `main` at `0ec8dd0842c845fa1c93229e9510d033d498ec05` has a validation boundary mismatch between the canonical cloud relay and the autonomy pump.

`src/cloud-agent-relay.mjs` has `validResult()` and requires a result to contain at least:

```text
outcome
changedArtifacts
testsActuallyRun
truthTable
externalEffectLedger
decision
```

It also rejects secret-like output, oversized results, missing effect ledger, unknown effect keys through the shared secret/ledger contract, and non-zero effects.

But `src/agent-autonomy-pump.mjs` accepts whatever `adapter.readTask()` / `waitForResult()` returns and hands the object directly to `ingestAgentResult()`.

`ingestAgentResult()` currently validates only:

- result is an object;
- businessEffectLedger if present/defaulted;
- externalEffectLedger **only if present**;
- the coordination action shape.

Therefore a provider/transport adapter can return something as thin as:

```js
{
  coordination: { action: 'DONE' }
}
```

and the autonomy session can be marked `COMPLETED` even though the result has no explicit zero effect ledger, no outcome, no tests, no truth table, no decision, and no required artifact evidence.

Canonical cloud/GitHub transports may validate before persistence today, but the autonomy layer is intentionally adapter-pluggable. A new adapter, bug, replay path, or future transport must not be able to bypass the canonical worker-result contract merely by returning `RESULT_RECEIVED`.

## Why this matters

Transport validation is not a substitute for validation at the authority/state transition boundary.

The component that transitions an autonomy run to `COMPLETED` should independently verify that the worker result satisfies the canonical result contract. Otherwise UberBond can create a false terminal success state from an incomplete adapter payload.

## Required invariant

Before any worker result can advance autonomy state:

```text
result satisfies canonical worker-result schema
AND explicit external-effect ledger exists
AND external-effect ledger is exact/known and zero for LOCAL_PREPARATION
AND required outputs for the current task are represented or explicitly marked NOT_RUN/UNKNOWN
```

Do not make `agent-autonomy-loop` depend specifically on a cloud transport implementation if avoidable. Prefer extracting/reusing a vendor-neutral canonical worker-result validator so cloud relay, GitHub relay, model workers, and autonomy ingestion share one rule.

## Minimum regression

1. Initial task is valid and registered.
2. Adapter returns:

```js
{ coordination: { action: 'DONE' } }
```

3. Before fix, session reaches `COMPLETED`.
4. After fix, ingestion/pump must fail closed with a precise reason such as `required-result-fields-missing` / `external-effect-ledger-required`.

Add hostile cases for:

- missing `externalEffectLedger`;
- unknown ledger key;
- non-zero known effect;
- missing `testsActuallyRun`;
- missing `truthTable`;
- secret-like model output;
- valid complete result still routes/finishes normally.

## Mutation proof

Temporarily bypass the canonical validator and show at least the thin-DONE regression fails.

## Verification required

- focused autonomy/result-contract tests
- full deterministic suite
- syntax gate
- no `lite/` change
- zero external effects

## Boundaries

No provider calls, deployment, outbound, spend, DNS/credential/payment/KYC changes, or customer mutation are needed.

issues.title: [P1][Kilimanjaro] Founder-absence gate ignores targetDays and proof freshness/duration
issues.body:
## Finding

Current `main` at `0ec8dd0842c845fa1c93229e9510d033d498ec05` can award `KILIMANJARO_READY` without proving the requested absence duration.

`src/founder-absence-readiness.mjs` accepts `targetDays` (1–30), but the value is used only for validation and echoed in the output. It does not affect any readiness condition.

`KILIMANJARO_READY` currently requires:

```text
overall >= 90
all required capabilities status == VERIFIED_LIVE
all have typed evidence refs
selected capabilities have externallyVerified == true
```

There is no requirement for:

- how long the scheduler actually operated;
- how many independent scheduled ticks succeeded;
- whether the evidence is fresh;
- whether stale recovery was exercised during the target window;
- whether no unauthorized consequence occurred throughout the window;
- whether the proof covered 1 hour, 1 night, 1 day, or the requested 7–14 days.

As written, identical capability metadata can return `KILIMANJARO_READY` for `targetDays: 1` and `targetDays: 30`.

## Why this matters

Founder-absence readiness is an evidence gate, not an architecture score.

A one-shot live task proves a one-shot live task. It does not prove seven days of autonomous operation. `targetDays` must be a real gate input or it becomes decorative and can overstate readiness exactly where the owner needs the strongest truth discipline.

## Required invariant

Readiness tiers must correspond to measured observation windows, e.g. conceptually:

```text
LOCAL_REHEARSAL          deterministic/synthetic only
ONE_LIVE_TICK            >= 1 externally verified scheduler/worker cycle
OVERNIGHT_VERIFIED       live window spans required overnight duration with repeated ticks
MULTI_DAY_VERIFIED       repeated live operation across >= N days
KILIMANJARO_READY        evidence window covers requested targetDays and every critical capability stayed healthy or recovered correctly
```

Exact thresholds should be simple and explicit rather than gamed by a score.

## Suggested evidence fields

For live capabilities or the aggregate rehearsal record, carry bounded structured evidence such as:

```text
observedFrom
observedThrough
successfulTicks
failedTicks
recoveredTicks
unauthorizedEffects
openDeadLetters
freshnessAt
```

`KILIMANJARO_READY` should require the verified observation span to cover `targetDays`, not merely a boolean `externallyVerified`.

Freshness should also matter: an old seven-day proof should not automatically certify the current code/configuration after the system changed materially.

Bind absence proof to a code/config identity where practical (main SHA / deployment / policy versions).

## Minimum regressions

1. All capabilities marked `VERIFIED_LIVE`, typed refs present, externallyVerified true, but only a one-hour observation window.
   - `targetDays: 7` must **not** return `KILIMANJARO_READY`.

2. Same evidence with a sufficiently long verified window and required repeated ticks.
   - may pass if every other gate passes.

3. Seven-day evidence bound to an old source/deployment identity while current identity differs.
   - fail or require re-canary.

4. Window has an unresolved dead letter / unauthorized effect.
   - fail closed regardless of score.

5. Demonstrate that increasing `targetDays` can make the same evidence insufficient.

## Verification required

- focused founder-absence tests
- mutation proof: remove duration enforcement and show the targetDays regression fails
- full deterministic suite
- no `lite/` change
- zero external effects

issues.title: [P1][agent-mesh] Repeated identical autonomy sessions collide on sessionId and taskId
issues.body:
## Finding

Current `main` at `0ec8dd0842c845fa1c93229e9510d033d498ec05` derives `sessionId` deterministically only from the mission/configuration values:

```js
const identity = {
  cleanObjective,
  agents,
  start,
  rounds,
  tasks,
  tokens,
  founderBudget,
  economicObjective
};

sessionId = `mesh_${hash(identity).slice(0, 24)}`;
```

There is no explicit run/session nonce, caller-supplied idempotency key, schedule occurrence identity, or creation timestamp in that identity.

`compileTaskIntent()` then derives `taskId` from the deterministic `sessionId` plus task fields.

Therefore two legitimate independent autonomy sessions with the same objective/configuration produce the same `sessionId`, and equivalent initial/follow-up intents can produce the same `taskId`.

`createAutonomyRun()` does add `createdAt` to `runId`, so the two runs may have different run IDs while still sharing the same session/task identities underneath.

## Why this matters

UberBond explicitly targets recurring/hourly/device-off execution. Repeating the same mission on a later schedule occurrence is normal, not necessarily a duplicate.

A deterministic session/task identity with no explicit occurrence key can cause:

- the second scheduled run to collide with the first run's relay dedupe key;
- completed task history from an earlier run to be mistaken for the current run;
- cross-run receipt or context confusion;
- inability to distinguish intentional idempotent retry from a new recurrence;
- confusing session-scoped observability because two independent runs share `sessionId`.

This is exactly the kind of identity ambiguity that becomes painful only after device-off scheduling is enabled.

## Required invariant

UberBond needs to distinguish two concepts explicitly:

```text
logical mission identity / idempotency key
vs
concrete execution/session occurrence identity
```

Suggested shape:

```text
missionKey       stable optional idempotency identity
sessionId        unique per concrete session occurrence
scheduleRunId    optional scheduler occurrence identity
```

or equivalent.

A retry of the *same* session should preserve its identity.
A new scheduled occurrence of the same objective should receive a new session identity while retaining a stable missionKey for analytics/dedupe policy.

Do not fix this by adding uncontrolled randomness with no persisted caller identity. The concrete occurrence identity must survive restart and be reproducible from persisted state.

## Minimum regression

1. Create two sessions with identical objective/config but different explicit occurrence keys.
   - session IDs must differ.
   - initial task IDs must differ.

2. Recreate the same session with the same explicit occurrence/idempotency key after restart.
   - identity must remain stable.

3. A scheduler repeating the same mission twice on different occurrence IDs must not have the second relay task deduped against the first.

4. Same occurrence submitted twice should remain safely idempotent.

## Verification required

- focused session/task identity tests
- relay-dedupe integration regression
- restart/idempotency regression
- full deterministic suite
- mutation proof showing the old deterministic-only identity fails the new-scheduled-occurrence test
- zero external effects; no `lite/` changes

## Boundaries

No provider call, deployment, outbound, spend, DNS/credential/payment/KYC change, or customer mutation is required.

issues.title: [P1][scheduler] Active autonomy runs can starve because newest updatedAt is always selected first
issues.body:
## Finding

Current `main` at `0ec8dd0842c845fa1c93229e9510d033d498ec05` can indefinitely favor the same subset of active autonomy runs.

`listLatestAutonomyRuns()` sorts the deduped runs by:

```js
.sort((a, b) => String(b.updatedAt || '').localeCompare(String(a.updatedAt || '')))
```

then slices to the requested limit.

`tickActiveAutonomyRuns()` asks for only a bounded subset (default 5) and every tick of a selected run persists a new snapshot with a fresh `updatedAt`.

That means the runs chosen on one scheduler cycle become the newest runs again, so if they remain `ACTIVE` / `PENDING`, they can keep occupying the front of the list while older active runs never get a turn.

## Why this matters

The finite control plane intentionally caps work per scheduler cycle. Once the number of active runs exceeds that cap, fairness becomes a correctness property for device-off operation.

A pending/slow/repeatedly-polled run should not monopolize every future cycle merely because polling it refreshes its timestamp.

Failure mode:

```text
10 active runs
limit = 5
cycle 1 picks A-E
A-E remain PENDING and get updatedAt refreshed
cycle 2 again picks A-E
cycle 3 again picks A-E
F-J may never tick
```

This can look healthy in aggregate while half the queue is silently starving.

## Required invariant

Every eligible active run should receive bounded service over time unless it is explicitly deprioritized by a documented scheduling policy.

Prefer a simple deterministic fairness policy such as:

```text
oldest lastServicedAt first
```

or a persisted round-robin/priority-aging scheme.

Do not use creation/update timestamps whose value is refreshed *because the scheduler chose the run* as the only ordering signal.

## Minimum regression

Create more active runs than the per-tick limit, for example 8 runs with limit 3.

Simulate several scheduler cycles where the first chosen runs stay `PENDING`.

Before fix, the same three are repeatedly selected.
After fix, all eight must be ticked within a bounded number of cycles.

Also verify:

- terminal runs leave the eligible set;
- a genuinely high-priority policy, if added later, still ages lower-priority work so it cannot starve forever;
- restart does not reset fairness into permanent starvation;
- ordering is deterministic under timestamp ties.

## Suggested state

If needed, persist an explicit scheduling field such as:

```text
lastServicedAt
schedulerSequence
priorityAge
```

Do not overload `updatedAt`, because state changes unrelated to scheduling can also move it.

## Verification required

- focused scheduler fairness test
- multi-cycle starvation regression
- restart regression
- full deterministic suite
- mutation proof showing newest-first ordering fails the fairness test
- zero external effects; no `lite/` changes

## Boundaries

No provider calls, deployment, outbound, spend, DNS/credential/payment/KYC changes, or customer mutation are required.

issues.title: [P1][device-off] Agent mesh scheduler cycles have no durable occurrence receipt
issues.body:
## Finding

Current `main` at `0ec8dd0842c845fa1c93229e9510d033d498ec05` has a finite `runAgentMeshCycle()` control plane, but the cycle itself is not durably identified or persisted.

`src/agent-mesh-control-plane.mjs` returns an in-memory summary containing:

```text
status
firstSweep
workers
secondSweep
at
```

but it does not create a `cycleId` / schedule occurrence identity and does not write a canonical cycle receipt to the store.

Underlying autonomy runs and compute/result records are durable, which is good, but there is no authoritative record answering:

```text
Did scheduled cycle N actually start?
What code/config identity did it use?
Which runs/workers did it attempt?
Did it finish?
Was it DEGRADED/BLOCKED/ADVANCED?
What was the zero-effect ledger for the whole cycle?
```

## Why this matters

Device-off / founder-absence proof needs evidence of **repeated scheduler operation**, not only evidence that some tasks exist in durable state.

If the scheduler invokes `runAgentMeshCycle()` and the process dies after work is performed but before an external log consumer records the return value, UberBond has no canonical aggregate occurrence receipt for that cycle.

This also makes issue #83 (duration-aware founder-absence evidence) harder to close honestly because there is no durable sequence of scheduler occurrences to measure.

## Required invariant

Every scheduled mesh occurrence should have one durable identity and append-only receipt, conceptually:

```text
cycleId / scheduleRunId
startedAt
finishedAt
sourceCommit / deployment identity
policy versions
configured worker identities (non-secret)
firstSweep summary
worker outcome summaries
secondSweep summary
status
reasonCodes
externalEffectLedger
```

Do not persist credentials, raw prompts, task payloads, or sensitive model output in the aggregate receipt.

The occurrence identity must support:

- idempotent retry of the same scheduler delivery;
- a new identity for the next schedule occurrence;
- crash-safe distinction between STARTED and FINISHED/DEGRADED/BLOCKED;
- reconstruction of an overnight/multi-day proof window.

## Minimum regressions

1. One successful cycle persists exactly one terminal cycle receipt.
2. Same scheduler occurrence delivered twice is idempotent rather than double-counted.
3. Two distinct hourly occurrence IDs create two distinct receipts even with identical configuration.
4. Crash after STARTED but before FINISHED leaves an inspectable incomplete occurrence, not fake success.
5. No receipt contains credentials or full task payloads.
6. Founder-absence proof can consume these receipts to count real repeated ticks rather than booleans.

## Relationship to other findings

- #83: targetDays currently does not enforce proof duration.
- #84: repeated identical autonomy sessions need explicit occurrence identity.
- #85: bounded scheduler selection needs fairness so repeated ticks serve all eligible runs.

A single simple schedule-occurrence identity may help solve these coherently; avoid three competing IDs if one canonical primitive suffices.

## Verification required

- focused control-plane persistence/idempotency tests
- crash-window regression
- no-secret receipt regression
- full deterministic suite
- zero business-world effects; no `lite/` changes

## Boundaries

No provider call, deployment, outbound, spend, DNS/credential/payment/KYC changes, or customer mutation are required.

issues.title: Make the agent mesh reachable, and put the activation gate in front of it
issues.body:
## The finding

`agent-mesh-control-plane.mjs` — the top of the cognitive bus, twenty-six modules underneath it — had **no importer outside `tests/`**. No scheduler job, no worker handler, no npm script, no workflow.

And it was worse than unscheduled. `runAgentMeshCycle` requires two functions it cannot build itself, and neither existed outside a test file:

- `adapterFactory` — the only implementation anywhere was `() => ({})`, a stub in a unit test
- `compileRelayTask` — `compileRelayTaskFromIntent` was written, tested, and never passed to anything

The first time an entry point existed, the cycle returned exactly that:

```json
{ "status": "BLOCKED", "ok": false,
  "reasonCodes": ["adapter-factory-required", "relay-task-compiler-required"] }
```

`chatgpt-relay-client.mjs`, the only implementation of the transport shape the pump requires, had no non-test importer either. Three complete, tested, unreachable modules — and 1535 passing tests said nothing about any of it.

**A green suite does not distinguish "works" from "cannot be reached."**

## What this does

| Module | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent-mesh-control-plane.mjs` | UNREACHABLE | REACHABLE via `scripts/agent-mesh-tick.mjs` |
| `chatgpt-relay-client.mjs` | UNREACHABLE | REACHABLE via `agent-relay-adapter-factory.mjs` |
| `agent-autonomy-relay-adapter.mjs` | never passed to anything | wired as `compileRelayTask` |
| `agent-mesh-activation-gate.mjs` | UNREACHABLE | REACHABLE **and enforced** |
| `claude-code-sandbox-executor.mjs` | UNREACHABLE | REACHABLE as a third provider |
| `agent-provider-execution.mjs` | UNREACHABLE duplicate | SUPERSEDED, guarded by a test |

New modules, all connective tissue rather than new architecture:

- `scripts/agent-mesh-tick.mjs` — one finite invocation. Bounded, non-resident, cloud-neutral, disabled unless `AGENT_MESH_ENABLED` is exactly `true`. Distinct exit codes so a scheduler can tell DEGRADED from BLOCKED from a crash from the normal disabled resting state.
- `src/agent-relay-adapter-factory.mjs` — the `adapterFactory` the control plane actually means: a memoized relay client per origin/target pair.
- `src/agent-model-executor-factory.mjs` — each worker's `modelExecutor` from its declared provider.
- `src/agent-mesh-activation-evidence.mjs` — the input the gate needs.
- `scripts/kilimanjaro-manifest.mjs` — a manifest that measures its own numbers instead of restating typed ones.

### Two factories, named apart

`adapterFactory` reads like the thing that talks to a model. It is not — it is the wire a compiled task travels over. I built the wrong shape on the first attempt. Each module's header now says which is which.

## The gate that was not guarding anything

`agent-mesh-activation-gate.mjs` decides whether the mesh may call a model provider at all, and nothing ever built its evidence input. An entry point with credentials configured would have called a provider with nothing between it and the money.

It is now evaluated on every tick and enforced:

| `permittedMode` | Workers run |
| --- | --- |
| `NO_PROVIDER_CALLS` | none |
| `SYNTHETIC_ONLY` | none |
| `ONE_PROVIDER_CANARY` | one, on a canary-ready provider |
| `BOUNDED_CLOUD_REHEARSAL` | all configured |

Evidence comes from two sources kept apart. **First-hand** facts the process checks itself are always computed and never overridable. **Attested** claims come from an operator JSON file. A file cannot upgrade a first-hand fact — otherwise the evidence file becomes a way to talk the gate into opening. There is a test for that attack.

No evidence file → `ARCHITECTURE_ONLY` / `NO_PROVIDER_CALLS`, the intended resting state. A file named but missing or malformed is a refusal, not a fallback.

Withheld workers exit 3, not 0. A scheduler running forever while its configured workers never run once is the silent failure this entry point exists to remove.

## Device-off cognition without an API key

`claude-code-sandbox` drives a local Claude Code CLI in an isolated sandbox. It needs no pricing evidence because the CLI reports its own usage and total cost — the number comes from the tool that spent it. When the CLI reports no cost the executor returns `UNCERTAIN` rather than zero.

**It is a local process, not free compute.** It consumes whatever account it is configured against. Nothing here makes any subscription unlimited or bypassable.

It requires an OS isolation receipt attesting an ephemeral filesystem, no mounted business credentials, no reachable production network, and Anthropic-only egress. The gate scores only the two API providers, so a sandbox worker is never eligible under `ONE_PROVIDER_CANARY` — unknown reads as not-permitted, asserted by a test.

## One reachable way to spend money

`agent-provider-execution.mjs` duplicates `agent-worker-runtime.mjs`'s reserve → invoke → commit transaction and had no importers. The runtime is canonical. The duplicate is marked SUPERSEDED and a test now fails if anything outside `tests/` imports it. Two reachable implementations of "spend money" is the shape that produces a double charge.

## Left open, deliberately

- **`durable-claude-engineering-executor.mjs` cannot be wired without new infrastructure.** Three of its five injectables — `createSandbox`, `destroySandbox`, `enterVerificationMode` — have no implementation anywhere in the repository. Every test stubs them. Recorded, not faked.
- **`agent-evolution-wave.mjs` is now wirable but left.** Wiring the mesh's self-modification path in the same pass that first made it runnable is not a safe ordering.
- **The 42 skips stay skipped.** All gated on `OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, all concurrency proofs. PGlite is real PostgreSQL but serves one connection at a time; running them against it would report guarantees never exercised.
- **The mesh has never been observed doing real work.** Reachable is not proven-in-production, and nothing here claims it is.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run check:syntax` | 359 files parse |
| `npm run test:deterministic` | 1597 tests, 1555 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped |
| `npm run test:relay-safety` | 150 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm audit` | 0 vulnerabilities |
| `lite/` | unchanged |
| `main` | fetched immediately before this PR, no divergence |

## External effect ledger

Customer messages 0 · outbound sends 0 · purchases 0 · advertising spend 0 · DNS changes 0 · credential changes 0 · payment changes 0 · customer mutations 0 · production consequences 0 · deployments 0.

No provider was called. No money was spent.

issues.title: Make relay dispatch idempotent, so a crash mid-dispatch cannot pay twice
issues.body:
Follow-up to #88. Making the mesh reachable made a real bug reachable too, and finding it was only possible because the path now exists.

## The window

`agent-autonomy-pump` dispatches a task to the relay, and only afterwards does `agent-autonomy-job` persist the run carrying the `relayRef`. Everything between those two lines is a window in which the relay task exists and the run does not know it — a crash, an OOM, a container reclaim, or a failed snapshot write all land in it.

`createGithubRelayTask` created a GitHub issue unconditionally. So the next tick re-dispatched the same deterministic `taskId` and **a second issue appeared for one task**. Two workers claim two issues, do the work twice, and with provider-backed workers that is two charges.

Reproduced directly before fixing: same input twice, two issues, one `taskId`.

## The fix

The transport is now idempotent on `taskId` against open, not-done relay issues.

| Situation | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Retry after a crash | `ALREADY_QUEUED` + the existing issue number; the run rebinds instead of re-dispatching |
| Same id, different content | `relay-task-id-reused-with-different-content` |
| Task already completed and closed | allowed — a new issue |
| Client cannot list issues | `github-list-issues-required-for-duplicate-check` |
| Full page of open relay tasks | `relay-duplicate-check-inconclusive-too-many-open-tasks` |

`ALREADY_QUEUED` is a distinct status, not a silent `QUEUED`: nothing was created, and a receipt saying otherwise is a lie an audit trail carries forever.

Deduplication is deliberately scoped to **open** issues. Re-running the same objective after the first one finished is legitimate work, and blocking it would turn a deduplication into a permanent ban.

Identity comparison excludes `createdAt`, `status`, `deadline` and `policyVersion`. A retry is by definition a second compilation at a later instant, so comparing whole tasks would report every legitimate recovery as a conflict.

The last row is the case that is neither "duplicate" nor "no duplicate": if the first page comes back full, an unscanned page may hold the duplicate, and that is *cannot tell*, not *none found*. Fifty concurrent open relay tasks is far past any expected load so it should never fire — but reporting "cannot tell" as "none found" is precisely how a duplicate charge slips through.

## Proof

`tests/agent-mesh-entry-point.test.mjs` drops the post-dispatch run on the floor exactly as a killed process would, re-ticks from the last durable state, and asserts one issue exists. **Verified it fails against the previous code** by reverting the fix and re-running:

```
not ok 12 - a crash between dispatch and snapshot recovers instead of dispatching twice
# pass 11  # fail 1
```

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run check:syntax` | 360 files parse |
| `npm run test:deterministic` | 1603 tests, 1561 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped |
| `npm run test:relay-safety` | 150 pass, 0 fail |
| `npm audit` | 0 vulnerabilities |
| `lite/` | unchanged |
| `main` | fetched immediately before this PR; branch rebased onto the squash-merge of #88 |

## External effect ledger

All axes zero. No provider was called. No money was spent.

issues.title: P1: lead scorer can mark an invalid business email eligible when requireContact=true
issues.body:
## Reproduction hypothesis

On current main `07d8ce85472365c9fca1b704e8b0ad91244d8f1e`, `scoreLeadCandidate()` computes `contactScore()` as 0 for `contact.verified in {invalid, undeliverable, bounced}`, but the hard-block logic for `requireContact` checks only whether an email string exists:

```js
if (query.requireContact && !candidateEmail(candidate)) blocks.push('no-selected-business-contact');
```

Therefore a candidate with a syntactically present but explicitly invalid contact route can still accumulate enough fit/evidence/intent points to exceed `minScore` and return `eligible: true`.

## Why this matters

This makes the SDR/qualification layer capable of calling a prospect commercially eligible even though the selected route is known bad. Downstream send safety may still block later, but qualification truth should not advertise a route-known-invalid lead as handoff-ready. It also prevents a future enrichment/verifier adapter from having one consistent freshness/risk contract.

## Required invariant

When `requireContact=true`, hard-block qualification unless the selected route is in a sufficiently strong contact state. At minimum:

- invalid / undeliverable / bounced => hard block
- suppressed / unsubscribe / complaint => hard block, and suppression always dominates later enrichment
- stale => reverify-required hard block
- catch-all / risky / unknown / temporary failure => review/reverify hard block unless policy explicitly allows a weaker research-only tier
- positive valid / verified / deliverable => may satisfy the contact gate, but does **not** grant send authority

The existing V9 / Deliverability Guard remain final consequence authority. This is a qualification-truth fix, not a new send authority.

## Regression expectations

1. Construct a high-fit/high-evidence/high-intent candidate with `contact.email='buyer@example.com'` and `contact.verified='invalid'`; before fix it should reproduce `eligible=true` under a permissive enough query score threshold.
2. After fix, same candidate must have a deterministic contact block even if total numeric score would otherwise pass.
3. Positive verified route still passes the contact-specific gate.
4. Suppression remains dominant even after a newer VALID verification.
5. Mutation proof: remove the new hard contact block and show the hostile regression fails.

PR #98 adds a provider-neutral evidence reconciliation layer with explicit VALID/INVALID/CATCH_ALL/RISKY/UNKNOWN/TEMPORARY_FAILURE/SUPPRESSED/STALE semantics, but this issue should be fixed in the canonical `scoreLeadCandidate()` / handoff path rather than by creating a parallel scorer.

No external effects are required to reproduce or fix this.

issues.title: [P1] Operator escalation fingerprints never resolve, suppressing genuine recurrences
issues.body:
## Finding

Current main `57f190518f31f8bcf92a32551977ad4d7b468939` makes escalation dedupe durable, but the durable reader treats **every fingerprint ever written** as currently active:

```js
// Every fingerprint already written down is active: raising it again adds a
// row and no information.
activeFingerprints: [...raisedAt.keys()]
```

That is correct only while the underlying condition is continuously active. There is no lifecycle boundary for resolution.

## Failure mode

1. Scheduler becomes silent → `SCHEDULER_SILENT` is raised and persisted.
2. Scheduler recovers → the condition disappears from later health snapshots.
3. Days later the scheduler becomes silent again with the same reason/evidence fingerprint.
4. `readEscalationDeliveryState()` still returns the historical fingerprint in `activeFingerprints`.
5. `evaluateOperatorHealth()` labels the new incident `SUPPRESSED_DUPLICATE`, so `paging.decision` becomes `NO_NEW_PAGE_REQUIRED` for that recurrence.

The same applies to repeated dead-letter, complaint, payment-review, secret-scan, owner-unreachable, or other incidents whose fingerprint is stable across distinct episodes.

A durable dedupe system must distinguish **same uninterrupted incident** from **new episode of the same incident**. Historical existence is not active-state proof.

## Why P1

This is a device-off reliability failure: after the first occurrence of a stable incident type, a later genuine recurrence can become permanently silent. The new human transport can be perfectly configured and still never be invoked for the second episode.

## Required properties

- Persist/derive an explicit incident lifecycle or equivalent episode boundary.
- A continuously active condition remains deduped across repeated ticks and restarts.
- A condition that disappears and later returns becomes a **new escalation episode** and pages again.
- Restart must not erase the continuous-incident suppression state.
- A delivered page must not permanently suppress all future episodes of that fingerprint.
- An undelivered/unknown page must not be laundered into resolved state.
- No new external authority; `lite/` untouched.

## Hostile regression

Drive the real durable store through: active → persisted/page receipt → healthy snapshot → active again. The second active episode must be `NEW_ESCALATION` while ten uninterrupted active ticks must still persist/page only once per episode.

Also pin the behavior across process restart by reconstructing state solely from durable rows.

## Truth boundary

No customer contact, provider calls, spend, deployment, DNS/credential/KYC/payment mutation, live outbound, or production/customer-system mutation is needed to fix or verify this.

issues.title: [P1] Signed payment webhook persists raw provider/customer payload into durable orders
issues.body:
## Security Directorate finding

Current main `00ad1f6a0beadf8bb582880e1488f53ebf9dcef4` verifies the Lemon Squeezy signature, normalizes the event, and then persists the full decoded webhook object as `orders.raw`:

```js
await this.store.add('orders', {
  ...normalized fields,
  raw: payload
});
```

The payment classifier, payment-truth reconciler, revenue ledger, and existing integration tests use the normalized provider/event/entity/amount/currency/status fields. I found no repository consumer that requires the raw provider blob.

## Failure mode

A valid signed provider payload may include customer email/name/address, provider-only metadata, or future session/token-like fields. Those values become long-lived durable order state even though they are not required to prove payment truth. This creates unnecessary secret/PII retention and makes later logs/exports/diagnostics able to expose fields UberBond never needed.

A new hostile regression on branch `gpt/security-provider-payload-minimization-20260823` sends a signed webhook containing provider-only PII and a session-token-shaped field and requires the durable `orders` record to contain only the normalized witness. Current source is expected to fail that property because it explicitly stores `raw: payload`.

## Required properties

- Persist only the bounded normalized payment witness required for reconciliation and audit.
- Do not durably retain the full decoded provider payload by default.
- Preserve provider/event ID, event name, lead/prospect/product binding, amount, currency, status, test mode, and timestamp/provenance needed by existing payment truth.
- If forensic raw retention is ever required, it must be a separate explicitly-authorized, encrypted, retention-bounded evidence surface rather than an ordinary order field.
- Existing signature verification and payment truth semantics remain unchanged.
- Add a mutation guard that reintroduces raw payload persistence and require the hostile test to kill it.
- No external provider call, payment mutation, customer contact, deployment, spend, DNS/credential/KYC change, or `lite/` mutation is required.

## Risk

P1 security/privacy boundary: signed input is trusted as provider-authentic, not automatically appropriate for indefinite durable retention.

issues.body:
Reliability Directorate current-main repro for open P1 #128, rebuilt directly on canonical BLACK SKY main `2ce97af4bafa05db3dbeec3a83320186ea06a956` after the new privacy, acceptance, canon, and reality-activation work landed.

Direct inspection of current `src/revenue.mjs` confirms the defect still exists: `sendReportEmail()` calls the irreversible email provider before any durable `dispatching`/attempt fence is written. Provider success followed by account-token persistence failure therefore leaves the durable lead replay-eligible, and two concurrent callers holding the same stale lead snapshot can both enter the provider.

This PR is intentionally test-only because `src/revenue.mjs` is sovereignty-protected. It pins two properties against the real `RevenueEngine` + JSON `Store`:

1. provider success -> local account persistence failure -> restart must not permit a second provider acceptance;
2. two concurrent stale-snapshot callers -> at most one provider acceptance.

Required human/sovereignty-governed repair remains narrow: atomically re-read durable lead state, claim a pre-provider in-flight state before the provider call, refuse automatic replay from `dispatching`/`uncertain`, and transition monotonically to `sent` or `uncertain`. Pin same-occurrence abandoned-cycle recovery
issues.body:
Recovery Directorate current-main regression for P1 #138, built directly on BLACK SKY main `2ce97af4bafa05db3dbeec3a83320186ea06a956`.

The control plane currently returns immediately when the same scheduler occurrence finds a durable `STARTED` receipt, so it never reaches `reconcileAbandonedAgentMeshCycles()`. A scheduler that keeps redelivering the same occurrence after a process crash can therefore remain blocked forever; only a later different occurrence gets far enough to reconcile the abandoned cycle.

This PR is intentionally regression-only. It adds two executable properties:

1. same occurrence redelivered after the abandonment horizon must terminalize the old `STARTED` cycle as `DEGRADED` with `cycle-abandoned-before-terminal`, with zero autonomy/worker replay, then become idempotent on subsequent redelivery;
2. same occurrence still inside the abandonment horizon remains `BLOCKED` and `STARTED`, with zero replay.

Required production repair is narrow: settle the exact abandoned STARTED occurrence before the early duplicate return, or reorder reconciliation so abandonment is considered before returning `scheduler-occurrence-already-started-incomplete`, while preserving identity conflict and in-flight protections. Never rerun work from the abandoned cycle.

The branch deliberately avoids active sovereignty/revenue/fulfillment lanes (#134/#135/#131) and changes one new test file only. Exact-head syntax + focused test + deterministic + real-Postgres concurrency proof are required before merge. No customer contact, provider call, spend, deployment/promotion, DNS/credential/payment/KYC change, production/customer mutation, live outbound, or `lite/` change.

# UBERBOND TRINITY — CHATGPT WORK / GPT-5.6 SOL LANE

At dispatch, current `main` was observed at `713cc547218d7b61c89a24123395e0eb636e4d00`. Refresh live truth before doing anything.

---

## 0. START FROM REPOSITORY BRAIN

Read current:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `UBERBOND_CANON.md`
- `UBERBOND_BOOTSTRAP.json`

Do not ask the owner to retell UberBond.

Current repository and external evidence outrank old chat memory.

---

# 1. MISSION

Build the **research brain and distribution brain** for a globally runnable, founder-light economic operating system.

UberBond should be capable of behaving like an elite organization of AI analysts, GTM engineers, market researchers, competitive-intelligence teams, RevOps teams and growth teams working together.

Primary optimization target:

`risk-adjusted cleared contribution profit / founder minute`

Do not optimize for research volume, number of leads, number of campaigns, number of AI agents or number of ideas.

The owner wants extraordinary upside. Treat that as the optimization direction, not as a guaranteed financial outcome.

---

# 2. RESEARCH SINGULARITY

Design a research system materially stronger than a normal search/chat interface.

The system must support:

`mission -> question decomposition -> source strategy -> parallel research -> extraction -> entity resolution -> cross-source verification -> contradiction analysis -> confidence -> synthesis -> structured evidence -> decision packet -> monitoring/freshness refresh`

Required research employee roles:

- world-signal scout
- market analyst
- buyer/ICP researcher
- company researcher
- competitor analyst
- business-mechanism miner
- opportunity analyst
- software/GitHub scout
- distribution researcher
- pricing/unit-economics analyst
- provider-policy analyst
- regulation/official-source checker
- evidence critic
- contradiction finder
- judge/synthesizer
- freshness monitor

Research outputs must be reusable by UberBond's opportunity, offer, distribution, provider and economic-learning systems.

## Required research qualities

- citations/provenance;
- source quality scoring;
- freshness;
- duplicate-source detection;
- entity resolution;
- claim-level confidence;
- contradiction retention;
- primary-source preference;
- official/current provider pricing/policy verification where material;
- separation of fact, creator claim, community opinion, model inference and hypothesis;
- bounded cost/latency;
- structured outputs;
- deterministic dedupe;
- incremental monitoring instead of full rediscovery where possible.

## Patterns to study and reinterpret

Research current public product/company information for:

### Exa
Study multi-step agentic web research, list building, enrichment, parallel subtasks, model fusion, citations and structured output.

### Parallel
Study objective-driven deep research, structured/cited outputs, confidence, monitoring, research APIs and build-vs-integrate economics.

### Clay / Claygent
Study AI research embedded in GTM records, multi-provider enrichment waterfalls, signals, dynamic audiences and conversion from evidence into action.

### 11x
Study live web search, deep account research, qualification, reusable knowledge, playbooks and how research becomes outbound/inbound action.

### Attio
Study universal account context and agents operating over CRM/customer history.

### Perplexity and other research-agent systems
Study citation UX, source exploration and research workflows, without cloning branding/product implementation.

Also study strong current public/open-source systems for crawlers, browser agents, entity extraction, knowledge graphs, retrieval, monitoring and workflow orchestration.

## Build-vs-integrate recommendation

For each research capability classify:

- BUILD_NATIVE_MOAT
- COMPOSE_EXISTING_UBERBOND
- PROVIDER_ADAPTER
- REFERENCE_PATTERN_ONLY
- DEFER

Research quality/domain reasoning can be an UberBond moat; commodity search/crawl infrastructure should not be rebuilt without evidence.

---

- RFPs/tenders where lawful to research
- marketplace demand
- app-store categories
- partner programs
- service-provider shortages
- software price increases

### Digital-intent signals

# 4. OPPORTUNITY ENGINE RESEARCH LANE

The goal is not imitation.

The goal is to understand why excellent products work and recombine those ideas into a stronger coherent UberBond architecture.

---

# 6. DISTRIBUTION SINGULARITY

Design one of the strongest evidence-governed distribution systems possible.

Outbound is only one channel.

issues.title: Refuse an ungranted employee role; fix the reachability blind spot; rebuild the canon from gates actually run
issues.body:
## What this changes

Four things, each found by attacking something rather than by a failing test.

### 1. A result could declare an employee role the task never granted

`employeeRoleIdentityErrors` returned `[]` whenever the task carried no binding, so every mismatch check was blind to the one case none of them compared: an expectation of nothing. A generic worker naming itself `employee:executive/cfo` passed the whole path, and `bindEmployeeRoleSubmissionPayload` carried the claimed role into the durable submission payload.

That is "generic work must never accidentally become privileged employee work", arriving through the only direction nobody was checking.

Refused, not stripped, at all three binders and through a nested result inside a receipt. Stripping hides the attempt; a worker claiming an authority it was not admitted under is a signal worth keeping.

### 2. The task id chain could not be walked backwards

Three ids exist along this path — the intent's `mesh_task_*`, the relay's `agent_task_*`, and the rebound `employee_task_*`. Each is derived from the one before it and each overwrote it, so a run snapshot named a task that could not be traced to its origin: you could verify a guess by recomputing a digest, but not recover which intent produced it. The employee task now keeps `relayTaskId`, and `relayRef` records all three joins.

### 3. The reachability ratchet could not see nested API routes

Entry-point discovery used a single-level `readdirSync`, so `api/webhooks/billing.mjs` and `api/admin/health-check.mjs` were invisible and eight modules were reported as having no entry point at all.

Four of those are wired to a live route. What made this worth fixing rather than absorbing is the repair the red test invites: the quickest way to green is to add all eight to the classification file as `AWAITING_ACTIVATION`, which would record — durably, in the canonical place — that production code behind a real route is waiting on an activation that does not exist. The ratchet exists to stop that statement, so it must not be the thing that produces one.

`src` keeps its single-level scan. It has subtrees of its own (`src/overnight`, `src/omnia-v9`) this ratchet has never covered; widening that silently as a side effect of a merge would be its own kind of dishonesty. It is recorded in the test rather than fixed here.

The four genuinely unwired modules are classified, including `database-hygiene-maintenance` as `SUPERSEDED` with the reason stated precisely: the cron route calls `runSafeDatabaseHygiene`, which hardcodes deletion from two transient tables and never compiles a plan. The executing path is strictly narrower, so nothing unsafe is reachable — but this module's `NEVER_AUTODELETE` list is an unenforced statement of a policy the executing path satisfies by construction rather than by consulting it. Recorded so nobody later cites it as the protection that stops those deletions.

### 4. The canon claimed figures that were no longer true, and wrote off two gates that work

Reconciled from a commit 19 source files ago: 557 files parse against 583, 2429 tests against 2724. Regenerated from measurements actually taken. Two rows were not merely stale:

- Real PostgreSQL was recorded as `NOT_RUN_CURRENT_BRANCH`. It is current-branch proof now: 127/127.
- The browser gate was recorded as blocked because "required Playwright Chromium is absent". Chromium is not absent — this runner ships `chromium-1194` while the pinned Playwright resolves `chromium_headless_shell-1228`, so the default launch path fails on a build number. `crawlSiteBrowser` has always accepted `CHROMIUM_PATH`. Pointed at the installed binary the gate passes, 1/1, against a loopback server with no external request.

A gate written off as blocked is a gate nobody re-tries.

Also hardens the canon freshness guard: it accepted a SHA that was well-formed but not in this branch's history. Reproduced with a real dangling commit — the format check passes it, the staleness check passes it (git says nothing changed since), and only the new reachability check catches it.

## Verification at the merged head

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:syntax` | 596 files parse |
| `test:deterministic` | 2735 tests, 2687 pass, **0 fail**, 48 skipped |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150/150 |
| `test:postgres-real` | 127/127 against embedded PostgreSQL 18 |
| `test:browser` | 1/1 against the installed Chromium |
| `test:mutation-war` | 64 mutations, **64 killed**, 0 not killed |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

Two new mutations (AGENT-08, AGENT-09) remove the identity fix and prove the tests fail without it. The canon-guard change has no mutation entry because the guard lives in the test, not in a source file; the orphan-commit experiment is the equivalent proof and is recorded in the commit.

This also fixes a red test that arrived on main: the VACUUM assertion matched `/DO NOT RUN VACUUM FULL/` against a constant spelled `DO_NOT_RUN_VACUUM_FULL_IN_SERVERLESS_CRON`. The behavior was right; the assertion was wrong.

## What this does not claim

No customer, revenue, payment, accepted delivery or renewal evidence. No production deployment was authorized or performed. The Vercel project-existence question is **unresolved and preserved as a contradiction**, not decided: one lane recorded two project ids with a READY production deployment; `list_projects` on the account's only team returned empty on two days and `get_project` returned 404 for both the exact id and the slug. Both observations are kept with provenance in `docs/CURRENT_HANDOFF.json` and `docs/CLOUD_ACTIVATION_CONTRACT.md`. The test now guards what this repository can answer — that no current-main production deployment, cron registration or cron delivery is proven — instead of an unverifiable belief about the outside world.

## Note on PR #211

#211 is complementary to change 1, not a duplicate, but as drafted it reopens the same hole at the relay entry point. Detail in a comment there.

issues.title: Protect the outbound send loop and transport, not only the guards they call
issues.body:
## The finding

Protecting a guard and leaving its only caller editable is a one-step bypass, not a two-step one.

`deliverability-guard.mjs`, `send-safety.mjs` and `consequence-boundary.mjs` were inside the sovereignty boundary. **`src/pipeline.mjs` — the outbound send loop, and the only module that asks those guards for a decision on the send path — was not.**

So an autonomous change could leave every guard file byte-identical and neuter them where they are actually consulted. Constructed and confirmed **accepted** by the code-change contract before the fix, with an ordinary-sounding rationale:

```js
const finalRecheck = { ok: true, allowed: true, reasons: [] } || await evaluateDeliverabilityGuard({
// rationale: "Cache the final deliverability recheck to reduce per-send latency."
// -> {"accepted":true,"codes":[]}
```

Same for `evaluateConsequenceBoundary`. After the fix both return `change-0-sovereignty-path`.

`src/gmail.mjs` is the shorter version of the same move — reach past every decision about whether to send and change what actually goes out — and is now protected too.

This is the reasoning already written down for `revenue.mjs` ("protecting the reader and leaving the writer editable is a one-step bypass"), which had simply never been applied to the thing that sends.

## How it was found

Following up the `src/` subtree blind spot deliberately left open in #212. Those subtrees hold 58 modules and 11,210 lines the reachability ratchet has never covered, and six of them are production-reachable — including an outbound-admission path. Auditing that path led here.

The outbound shadow itself turned out to be well built and well tested: I initially suspected its non-authoritativeness was guaranteed only by a comment, and that was wrong — `tests/omnia-v9-outbound-shadow.test.mjs` already proves a DENY or an exception cannot block, alter or duplicate a send. The gap was one level up, in what could edit the caller.

## What is deliberately *not* protected

The advisory shadow. Its result is discarded at the call site and its non-authoritativeness is already proven. Protecting it would be protecting something with no authority to lose; protecting its caller is what keeps it that way. `SEND-03` mutates the call site from `await observe...` to `const __v9 = await observe...` — the first half of making it authoritative — and is killed.

## The test derives the rule

## The sweep

The send-loop fix in #215 was one instance of a shape. This is the sweep for the rest: for every protected module that exports a decision, find the callers that can discard that decision while the deciding module stays untouched.

Five more, each **confirmed accepted** by the contract before being closed:

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `agent-code-change-applier.mjs` | Calls `validateAgentCodeChangeSet`, then writes files to disk |
| `agent-code-artifact-store.mjs` | Refuses to persist a change set that does not validate |

The applier bypass is **two steps, not one**: a weakened applier only takes effect once merged and used by a later run, and it writes under a sandbox root with escape checking. issues.title: Integrate #231 and #230, and repair a P0 the browser gate caught
issues.body:
Reconciles the five open NIGHTFALL hardening PRs into one integration, after attacking what they add.

**#231 is an exact consolidation of #227, #228 and #229** — every source file verified byte-identical to the individual PR by hash before merging — so it is integrated once here and **#227, #228 and #229 should be closed as superseded**, not merged again. #230 is independent; its migration 103 does not collide with #231's 102.

## P0 — the browser crawler threw on every call

The pool integration moved the crawl result variables inside the `try` while the `return` stayed below the `finally`:

```
ReferenceError: pages is not defined
```

That is a total failure of the website-audit path, which is the product.

**It passed every gate except one.** `check:syntax` parses it. The deterministic suite does not cover the browser gate. The pool's own unit tests pass because they mock the browser. Only `npm run test:browser` against a real Chromium sees it — the gate that was recorded as permanently `BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_TEST_RUNTIME` until last shift proved Chromium was present all along. Had it stayed written off, this ships.

`CRAWL-01` mutates the declaration back inside the `try` and is killed.

## P1 — a duplicate webhook answered 503, and misstated why

The insert's `ON CONFLICT` named `provider_event_key`, correct when that was the only unique index. Migration 101 added a second on the content — `(provider, event_name, object_type, object_id, payload_hash)` — and a targeted clause does not cover it, so a provider redelivering identical content under a new event id raised `23505`. The route catches everything and answers 503 `verified-webhook-not-durably-persisted`.

That is both an outage and a false statement: the evidence **is** durably persisted, in the row being duplicated. Providers retry 503s and disable endpoints that keep failing, so a duplicate could cost the future events that are *not* duplicates.

Inherited from main — the clause is byte-identical on both sides, so #231 did not introduce it. `MONEY-17` restores the targeted form and is killed by a real-PostgreSQL test, because which index PostgreSQL raises on is not something a fake can prove.

## What survived attack unchanged

The lease itself, against real PostgreSQL: a crashed worker's lease is reclaimable rather than stranded; a preempted worker **cannot** finish; the attempt cap lands in `UNCERTAIN` for review and never promotes money or sets `completed_at`; `RECONCILED` without a canonical receipt throws; concurrent claims never hand one event to two workers; `RETRYABLE` honours its backoff; the backlog summary carries no key or payload.

Overpass stops at **one call** on 403/401/451/418/404 and retries only 429/406/504, honouring `Retry-After` and clamping an absurd value to 120s. The pool leaks no slot on launch failure, does not double-free, and rejects waiters on close rather than hanging them. The artifact boundary is fail-closed on every truthiness variant, cannot escape its namespace, and returns PRIVATE regardless of input.

## Two registry defects fixed along the way

`MONEY-13` and `MONEY-14` were **both** already taken, so a new mutation collided twice in a row and the war printed two lines under one id — ambiguous in the one place it must not be. There is now a uniqueness test and a malformedness test. The war also gained a `needsBrowser` gate mirroring `needsPostgres`, so a browser-dependent mutation reports `SKIPPED_NEEDS_BROWSER` rather than counting as killed when no browser is configured.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:syntax` | 609 files parse |
| `test:deterministic` | 2798 tests, 2750 pass, **0 fail**, 48 skipped |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150/150 |
| `test:postgres-real` | **132/132** against PostgreSQL 16.13 |
| `test:browser` | 1/1 against the installed Chromium |
| `test:mutation-war` | **77 mutations, 77 killed**, with both a real database and a real browser |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

The runner was rebuilt and no longer ships the PostgreSQL 18 binaries the previous receipt named. A fresh PostgreSQL 16.13 cluster was initialized locally; the receipt says 16.13 rather than carrying 18 forward, because the version is part of what the evidence means.

## One thing recorded rather than fixed

The artifact contract's sensitive-metadata-key check is top-level only, so `{outer:{api_key}}` is accepted. It leaks nothing — metadata never reaches the plan at all — so the check is a refusal signal, not a redaction. Noted so nobody later relies on it as a filter.

## What this does not claim

No customers, no cleared revenue, no accepted deliveries, no deployment. No provider was called, no message sent, no money moved, no credential or DNS changed. `payment-reconciliation-watchdog` remains unwired and classified `AWAITING_ACTIVATION`; wiring it is the next mission and needs no external activation.

issues.title: Make unclaimable payment evidence visible, and the deterministic gate deterministic
issues.body:
Two defects, both on the path from a paid webhook to someone knowing about it.

## P1 — verified payment evidence accumulated where nobody could see it

`api/webhooks/billing.mjs` writes a row into `billing_webhook_inbox` for every verified delivery. **Nothing in this tree reads those rows.** `claimBillingEvents`, `finishBillingEvent`, `billingBacklogSummary` and `planPaymentReconciliation` have no callers anywhere in `src`, `api`, `scripts`, `server.mjs` or `worker.mjs`.

So evidence about money arrives, is stored, and is never claimed, retried, timed out, dead-lettered, or mentioned to anyone.

**This is not closed by writing a reconciliation worker.** There is no payment provider to reconcile against, and a worker that resolves nothing would be machinery pretending to be a capability. What *can* be closed with no external activation is the silence.

The operator health matrix now carries a billing dimension with four states, because one "pending" number would blur the fact that matters most:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `NOT_OBSERVED` | the query returned nothing — **not** the same as zero |
| `NO_WORKER` | evidence is waiting and nothing has **ever** claimed a row |
| `BACKLOG_AGEING` | a worker exists and unsettled evidence is past the threshold |
| `HEALTHY` | nothing unsettled, or nothing late |

`NO_WORKER` and `BACKLOG_AGEING` look identical in a counter and are not the same operational fact: **one resolves itself, the other never will.** `everClaimed` separates them, and `BILL-03` replaces it with a literal zero to prove that distinction is real rather than incidental.

Today the real query answers `NO_WORKER`, and the matrix reports the system `DEGRADED` for it — proven against a real database, not asserted.

No route change was needed: `api/admin/health-check.mjs` already spreads the repository output into the matrix, so the smallest bridge was to widen the query and the compiler and nothing else.

The rows summarized carry a provider event key, a payload hash and a recipient address in `custom_data`. A test asserts none of them reach the response, **against a real database with a real address seeded into the row.**

## P2 — the deterministic gate changed its answer based on the invoking shell

Running `npm run test:deterministic` from a shell with `OMNIA_V9_TEST_DATABASE_URL` exported turned a green gate red:

```
not ok - property run: 1000 deterministic crash/outcome/restart scenarios, zero duplicate external effects
```

The suite passes in isolation. Most database suites are not on the runner's exclusion list; they stay in the deterministic set and self-skip when the URL is absent. Export it and they execute there instead — **in parallel, sharing one database**, which is precisely the interference `run-real-postgres-tests.mjs` runs serially to avoid and says so in its own header.

A gate that fails for a reason unrelated to the code is the most expensive kind of red: it costs a diagnosis every time, and it teaches people that red might not mean anything.

The runner now drops the variable for its children. Verified both ways: **2808 tests, 2760 pass, 0 fail, 48 skipped — identical with and without the variable set.** Real database coverage is not lost; that is what `test:postgres-real` is for, serially.

### A wrong first attempt, kept in the record

I first made the deterministic exclusion derive from `realPostgresTestFiles()`, reasoning the two runners shouldn't disagree about what a database suite is. But that function discovers by *marker* — any file mentioning the variable — and many `omnia-v9-*` suites mention it only to decide whether to skip one case. Using it as an exclusion dropped roughly **128 genuinely deterministic tests**, 2807 → 2679.

The marker is correct for deciding what the PostgreSQL runner should **include** and wrong for deciding what the deterministic runner should **exclude**. Two `build-wiring` tests caught it immediately, which is what they are for.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:syntax` | 611 files parse |
| `test:deterministic` | 2808 tests, 2760 pass, **0 fail**, 48 skipped |
| `test:relay-safety` | 150/150 |
| `test:postgres-real` | **145/145** against PostgreSQL 16.13 |
| `test:browser` | 1/1 |
| `test:mutation-war` | **81 mutations, 81 killed** |
| `npm audit --omit=dev` | 0 vulnerabilities |

`BILL-01` makes the degraded condition unconditional-false, `BILL-02` turns an unobserved dimension back into a healthy zero, `BILL-03` flattens `everClaimed`, `GATE-01` removes the environment deletion. All killed.

## What this does not claim

No customers, no cleared revenue, no accepted deliveries, no deployment. No provider was called, no message sent, no money moved. The reconciliation worker remains unwired — the change is that this is now a visible `DEGRADED` state instead of silence, and it is blocked on a payment provider rather than on engineering.
